With Always on top enabled, Task Manager shows as a floating window above other apps, so you can watch processes and resource usage while using other apps.

Note: the floating window is created only at startup and leaves gaps on all four edges, so the system and other apps stay reachable. To go back to the normal UI, turn off Always on top and restart the app; there is no need to revoke this permission.
Always on top has been saved. Tap Restart to restart the app now; it reopens as a floating window. Tap Cancel to undo this change: the setting is not saved and the UI stays as it is.

Injects test devices that carry no data into the performance page: one more per tap, and the matching entry shows up immediately (test disks go to “Disk N”, test adapters to “WLAN”, test GPUs to “GPU N”). It does not affect real capture; the clear button removes them all at once.

When checked, every network adapter in the low-level snapshot is registered as a performance page device, including ones normally hidden: p2p0, an unconnected wlan0, an rmnet carrying only fe80::, the VPN tun0, and so on. They still have no data (details show “Not supported”, rate is 0). The switch lasts only for this run and resets when the app restarts. Devices the low level never captured, such as the loopback lo, do not appear just because the box is checked.

Use accessibility permission to stay on top
For debugging system windows: draws above them through accessibility. Works only together with Always on top, which then needs no overlay permission.

With this option on, Task Manager draws its window above system windows through the accessibility service, which is what you need when debugging system windows. On its own it creates no window: Always on top must be on as well.

Note: revoking the accessibility permission only turns this option off. If overlay permission is still granted, Always on top keeps running as a normal floating window; both are turned off only when overlay permission is also missing.

Accessibility permission was not granted, so this option cannot be enabled for now.\nTap Try again to reopen the system accessibility page; tap Cancel to leave everything unchanged and keep the option off.
Task Manager - Accessibility window on top
Lets Task Manager place its window above system windows for debugging them. Only used when the accessibility top option in the app is on.
